title: Steward ledger and migration-safe prompt canonicalization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a steward ledger and canonicalization flow for curated prompt banks so that prompt migrations and config/model changes are traceable, replayable, and safe to roll back. The goal is to ensure every prompt artifact used by evals has a provenance record, immutable fingerprint, and a migration plan that preserves gating for quality regressions when model/config rollouts occur.
acceptance_criteria: Every prompt artifact in curated banks has an immutable fingerprint (hash) recorded in the steward ledger
Migration tooling can map old prompt fingerprints to new canonicalized prompts and produce a delta report
CI gates can replay a historical eval snapshot using the canonicalized prompts to verify no regression introduced by config/model change
Permissions for who can mark a prompt as 'canonical' are enforced (RBAC) and appear in the ledger entry
A lightweight UI (Console) view exists to inspect prompt provenance and migration diffs
Automated backfill job can generate ledger entries for existing curated banks without blocking rollout
steps: Design ledger schema: fingerprint, author, steward, canonical_version, predecessor_fingerprint, rationale, linked PR/Confluence
Prototype CLI to compute fingerprints and emit ledger entries for a single prompt file
Build migration mapping tool that aligns prompts by similarity heuristics and manual overrides
Integrate ledger write into prompt curation flow and PR checks
Add a replayable eval snapshot exporter that pins model/config + prompt fingerprint set
Implement minimal Console read UI for inspection and diff visualization
Run backfill job for current curated banks and validate with spot checks
Create CI gating step to fail a rollout if replayed snapshot shows regression beyond threshold
decisions: Use SHA256 over normalized prompt text (trim spaces, normalize unicode, remove stable metadata) as the canonical fingerprint
Ledger will be append-only and stored in internal object store + searchable index; edits are handled via new ledger entries referencing predecessor fingerprints
Similarity matching for migrations will be hybrid: lexical normalization + cosine on embedding vector; human steward must confirm above a configurable confidence threshold
Permission model leverages existing RBAC groups (prompt-stewards, eval-engineers, reviewers) instead of building a new ACL system initially
Replayable snapshots will reference exact model build id + runtime config + prompt fingerprints to guarantee determinism for gating
comments: 2026-03-02 Miguel Santos: Started prototype CLI; computing fingerprints on curated prompts shows ~120K unique items across banks. Initial run attached: gs://redwood-dev/prompt-fingerprints/2026-03-02.csv

2026-03-04 Priya Narang (PM): Prefer adding a 'rationale' field when steward marks a prompt canonical — helps downstream auditors. Also request a short UI stub for stewards to approve mapping decisions.

2026-03-05 Design review (Xia Chen): Visual diff mockups uploaded to Figma (link below). UX calls for side-by-side render with whitespace-insensitive diff and a small editor to propose canonicalization edits.
2026-03-07 Infra note (Diego Alvarez): Ledger append workload should be low QPS but needs retention policy. Proposing 7 years cold storage and 90-day hot index for quick search.

2026-03-09 Engineering update: Migration mapping prototype flagged 2.2% false positive mappings for near-duplicate prompts with templated slots. Plan: require human approval for any mapping where normalized-lexical similarity < 0.95.

2026-03-10 QA (Lina Garcia): Replay snapshot harnessed against model v3.2 showed a 0.6% regression on the 'answer-fidelity' metric for one curated bundle. Filing follow-up ENG-84247 to triage eval noise vs regression.
